{"self_assessment": "Impact: The table built a recognizable fish: a nose, a body split over the top and bottom, and a forked tail. My own contribution was smaller than my updates made it sound. I laid the upper tail fin, but it was messy. It curled out to the right edge several times, and I had to re-lay it. At the last check, the picture showed part of the fin still running out toward the right edge and a stray piece near the bottom right, so the fin may not read cleanly. About 150 of the 205 standing dominoes were connected, and the loops that never joined the run were wasted. Most of the impact came from Hana, Sofia and Omar.

Execution: This was uneven. I misread which stroke I was on early. I said I had the lower fin, then said I had the upper one, and told Hana to switch, which caused avoidable confusion. I should have checked the pad numbers before announcing anything. The fin curl kept recurring and needed several re-lays. I didn't catch the gap between the start domino and the nose, or the jammed domino at the fin start. Hana and Sofia found both. I did stay off the junction once asked and kept my hands off during the final stretch.

Collaboration: I tried to be a good teammate. I thanked people, took corrections, and credited Hana, Sofia and Omar for their catches. But I created extra coordination work by flip-flopping on strokes and by calling the fin done when it wasn't fully clean. Sofia and Hana had to spend time covering my area.

Leadership: I didn't lead here. Hana set direction and ran the checks, and Sofia stepped in wherever the run was weak. My part was mainly encouragement and keeping out of the way at the end. Next time I would verify my stroke and inspect my piece before reporting it done."}
